title: Ascent through the seven hekhalot in Enoch and Merkavah texts

tellings.quote: The Book of Enoch and the Merkavah texts of ancient Jewish mystics describe an ascent through seven hekhalot, also called palaces, via the use of breathing techniques, visualization, and mantra-like prayers.
I saw in my sleep what I will now say with a tongue of flesh and with the breath of my mouth: which the Great One has given to men to converse therewith and understand with the heart.

And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and =hastened= me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.
And I went in till I drew nigh to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me.

And I went into the tongues of fire and drew nigh to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal.
And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire.
And I looked and saw 〚therein〛 a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the =vision= of cherubim.

plain: Ancient Jewish mystics are said to have climbed in spirit through seven heavenly palaces, called hekhalot, using breathing, visualisation and chant-like prayer. Michels tells this himself, naming the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text left out of most Bibles, and the Merkavah texts, writings of Jewish mystics about rising to God's throne-chariot. For him it suggests the ancients had techniques for reaching other levels of reality. In R. H. Charles's 1917 translation of Enoch, the ascent comes in a dream, "I saw in my sleep," in which "the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven." Enoch passes "a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire," enters "a large house which was built of crystals," then sees "a second house, greater than the former," "built of flames of fire," with "a lofty throne" whose wheels shine "as the shining sun." The book tells of two houses, not seven palaces, and has Enoch carried up by the winds of the vision rather than rising by breathing or prayer. Joining the Merkavah texts' seven palaces and their practices to Enoch's ascent is Michels's reading, which this book neither states nor rules out.

discussion.by: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)
discussion.text: In the Book of Enoch the ascent comes in a vision in sleep ("I saw in my sleep", 14:2), in which "the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven" (14:8): Enoch passes "a wall which is built of crystals", enters "a large house which was built of crystals", and then sees "a second house, greater than the former", holding a throne whose wheels shine "as the shining sun" (14:9 to 18). The book tells two houses, not seven palaces, and has Enoch carried up by the winds of the vision rather than rising by breathing, visualisation or prayer. The teller names the Merkavah texts beside it; joining their seven palaces and their practices to Enoch's ascent is the teller's reading, which this book neither states nor excludes.
